review_notes: I read the whole target file and searched the Tim81 and Timmesfeld directories for repeats of its blocks. The duplicated machinery I found is the "end vectors e₀ and e_last are isotropic" package. It is re-proved inline in UnitaryTIModule.lean and UnitaryTIModuleTI.lean, which proves it twice. It is also re-proved in UnitaryTIModuleSU.lean and UnitaryTIModuleEven.lean, which proves it twice. The same facts appear as private lemmas in Sec7/LinePairFrame.lean and as inline haa/hdd in Sec7/AutCentralizer.lean. The pieces are short, but the repetition is exact and wide. A public lemma already exists in ModelSUBlock for the companion fact uForm_single_zero_last. I did not make separate findings for the hA/hB duplication in the even branch, for commSpan_map, or for the odd/even case split. The first is a short two-fold repeat, and I found no other copy of the other two. I could not compile anything. The proposed lemma names are new, so any replacement is untested. Possible name clashes and import placement are unchecked.

findings.problem: The proof re-derives that the end indices 0 and Fin.last (m+1) are not fixed by Fin.rev, then uses them to show uForm vanishes on Pi.single 0 1 and on Pi.single (Fin.last (m+1)) 1. The same sequence is copied inline in UnitaryTIModuleTI.lean (twice), UnitaryTIModuleSU.lean and UnitaryTIModuleEven.lean (twice). Sec7/LinePairFrame.lean proves the same facts as the private lemmas uForm_single_zero_self and uForm_single_last_self. Sec7/AutCentralizer.lean proves them inline as haa and hdd. Each copy has to carry the same `rw [Fin.rev_zero]; intro h; congrArg Fin.val; simp` argument, which has several steps. The result is at least six separate proofs of two facts. A public lemma that is already used, uForm_single_zero_last, covers only the pairing of the two ends.
findings.proposed_change: Add public lemmas next to uForm_single_zero_last in CFSG/Timmesfeld/Transvection/ModelSUBlock.lean (namespace ModelRank, which this file already opens). The exact statements are `uForm σ (Pi.single (0 : Fin (m + 2)) 1) (Pi.single 0 1) = 0` and `uForm σ (Pi.single (Fin.last (m + 1)) 1) (Pi.single (Fin.last (m + 1)) 1) = 0`, stated for a general σ and general m. The proofs are the existing one-liners from LinePairFrame: `uForm_single_self (by rw [Fin.rev_zero]; exact zero_ne_last)` and `uForm_single_self (by rw [Fin.rev_last]; exact zero_ne_last.symm)`. Alternatively, prove `(0 : Fin (m+2)) ≠ Fin.rev 0` and `Fin.last (m+1) ≠ Fin.rev (Fin.last (m+1))` once and call them everywhere. In `unitaryTIModule`, delete h0r and hLr and set `he₀ := uForm_single_zero_self` and `heL := uForm_single_last_self`. The `ne_rev` arguments that exists_mem_sup_conjSub_eq, uForm_single_self and the others take can be supplied from the same lemmas. UnitaryTIModuleTI, UnitaryTIModuleSU and UnitaryTIModuleEven get the same treatment. LinePairFrame drops its private copies and AutCentralizer replaces haa and hdd with the shared lemmas. In the target, zero_ne_last comes from an unopened namespace, so the shared lemma should live where it is already in scope (ModelSUBlock) rather than in the target file.
findings.benefit: The same short non-trivial argument is proved once instead of at least six times. Each caller loses about 10–12 lines of boilerplate and the unitaryTIModule proof gets shorter. A change to how Fin.rev is handled, or to the phrasing of the isotropy hypotheses, is then made in one place. The private duplicate lemmas in LinePairFrame go away.
